offence_severity: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
physical_harm: No injuries or death caused other than the suicide by hanging
number_of_offences: Charged under one count under Section 306 IPC; upheld by Trial Court and High Court
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the FIR lodged by the mother of the deceased and the statement of the colleague of the deceased, but found no proximate link between the marital dispute and the commission of suicide.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the complainant and the colleague of the deceased but found that their statements did not establish any instigation or active role by the appellant in the deceased's suicide.

legal_representation.accused: Anand Dilip Landge, Paras Yadav, Mrs. Sangeeta. S. Pahune. Patil, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Shrirang B. Varma, Siddharth Dharmadhikari, Aaditya Aniruddha Pande, Bharat Bagla, Sourav Singh, Aditya Krishna, Ms. Preet S. Phanse, Adarsh Dubey, K.K.L. Gautam, Ms. Vaishali Nariyala, Manoj Sharma, Madan Sagar, Rajbeer, Sanjeev Malhotra, Advs.

investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed on 04.11.2020, Sessions Case No. 100 of 2021 registered and pending

appeal_history.supreme_court: Allowed appeal, set aside High Court order, allowed discharge application on 10 July 2024

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant-accused abetted the deceased's suicide through harassment, beating, and other acts, including sending vulgar messages and insisting the deceased not visit his parents, which led to the deceased's suicide.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no active role or positive act by the appellant to instigate or aid the deceased in committing suicide, and that the deceased may have committed suicide due to his own issues, such as alcohol addiction.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for a conviction under Section 306 IPC, there must be clear mens rea, an active or direct act leading the deceased to commit suicide, and a proximate link between the accused's conduct and the suicide.
precedent_relied_upon: S.S. Chheena v. Vijay Kumar Mahajan [2010] 9 SCR 1111 : [2010] 12 SCC 190; Amalendu Pal v. State of W.B. [2009] 15 SCR 836 : [2010] 1 SCC 707; Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh [2001] Supp. 4 SCR 247 : [2001] 9 SCC 618; Gurucharan Singh v. State of Punjab [2020] 8 SCR 741 : [2020] 10 SCC 200
